title: Decode Ways
summary: Count the ways a string of digits can be read as letters when A = 1 through Z = 26.

tests.explain: It can be read as 1, 2 ("AB") or as 12 ("L"): two ways.
2 2 6, 22 6 and 2 26 are all valid: three ways.
A leading 0 cannot be decoded, and "06" is not allowed as a two-digit code: zero ways.

hints: Letters map to the numbers 1 to 26. A digit can be read alone (1 to 9), or two digits together can be read as one letter (10 to 26). A 0 can never stand alone.
Let ways[i] be the number of ways to decode the first i characters. The last letter is either one digit or two digits, so ways[i] combines ways[i - 1] and ways[i - 2] when those readings are valid.

ways[0] = 1 (empty string). For position i: if s[i-1] is not '0', add ways[i-1]. If the two-digit number s[i-2..i-1] is between 10 and 26, add ways[i-2]. Return ways[n]; only the last two values are needed.
